The method relates to an electric power control process in which switching elements are controlled on the basis of a carrier wave and a duty command value. In this method, an electric current is first measured, and a command value is calculated based on the measured current. The calculated command value is then used to operate the switching elements so that electric power is controlled in accordance with a desired output.

The method further includes determining whether an operation period of the switching elements should be extended beyond one cycle of the carrier wave. When it is determined that the operation period is to be changed, the control process adjusts the switching operation so as to reduce unnecessary switching.

In particular, during the first half cycle of the carrier wave after the operation period has been changed, the number of switching operations is reduced. This helps suppress switching losses and improves the efficiency of the electric power control process.

During an intermediate period following the first half cycle, the slope of the carrier wave is changed. The modified carrier wave is then compared with the duty command value, and the switching elements are controlled according to the result of this comparison. By changing the slope of the carrier wave in this intermediate period, the method enables smooth control while maintaining consistency with the calculated duty command value.

The method also reduces switching operation during the last half cycle of the carrier wave. As a result, switching losses can be further decreased, and stable power control can be maintained even when the operation period is extended beyond a single carrier-wave cycle.
outputs.L4:
An electric power control method is provided for controlling an inverter that converts electric power by switching a plurality of switching elements in accordance with pulse-width modulation. In this method, a current flowing through the inverter, a load, or an electric motor connected to the inverter is measured, and a control device calculates duty commands on the basis of the measured current and a target power, voltage, torque, or current value. The duty commands represent switching instructions to be used in comparison with a carrier wave, such as a triangular wave or sawtooth wave, for generating gate signals for the switching elements of the inverter.

The control device determines, for each control period, whether inverter operation should be performed within a normal operation period corresponding to one cycle of the carrier wave or whether the operation period should be extended beyond one carrier-wave cycle. When the operation period is not extended, the inverter is controlled in a normal pulse-width modulation manner by comparing the duty commands with the carrier wave and switching the inverter elements according to the comparison result.

When the control device determines that the operation period should be extended, the operation period is divided into a first half-cycle period, an intermediate period, and a last half-cycle period. During the first half-cycle period and the last half-cycle period, the comparison behavior between the carrier wave and the duty commands is modified so that unnecessary switching is suppressed or reduced. For example, switching states may be held for a longer time, or a comparison threshold may be adjusted so that fewer transitions occur. As a result, the number of turn-on and turn-off operations of the switching elements is decreased in portions of the extended period where switching reduction is most effective.

During the intermediate period between the first and last half-cycles, the slope of the carrier wave is changed so that the desired duty relationship is maintained despite the extension of the operation period. By modifying the inclination of the carrier wave, the control device can continue to generate appropriate switching commands while compensating for the time extension. This allows the inverter output voltage or current to remain close to the commanded value, even though the number or timing of switching events has been altered.

Accordingly, the method reduces switching losses and electromagnetic noise caused by frequent switching of the inverter elements. At the same time, because the duty commands are still calculated from measured current values and the carrier-wave comparison is adjusted during the extended period, the inverter can maintain stable power control. The method is therefore useful for applications such as motor drives, power converters, electric vehicles, and other systems in which it is desirable to improve efficiency, reduce heat generation, and suppress noise without significantly degrading control performance.

**An Electric Power**

An electric power system is an essential part of modern life. It provides the energy needed to run homes, schools, hospitals, factories, and transportation systems. Without electric power, many daily activities would become difficult or impossible, such as lighting rooms, charging phones, using computers, and operating machines.

Electric power is produced in different ways. It can come from power plants that use coal, natural gas, nuclear energy, water, wind, or sunlight. Renewable sources like solar and wind power are becoming more popular because they are cleaner and help reduce pollution. After electricity is generated, it travels through power lines to reach cities, towns, and villages.

An electric power supply must be reliable and safe. If there is a power outage, it can affect businesses, communication, and emergency services. For this reason, engineers work hard to improve electrical grids and make them stronger and more efficient.

In the future, electric power will become even more important. As electric cars, smart homes, and new technologies continue to grow, the demand for electricity will increase. Using energy wisely and supporting clean power sources can help create a better and more sustainable world.

counterfactuals.output:
1. **An electric power control method** for controlling electric power supplied through a power conversion circuit including a switching element, the method comprising:  
   generating a carrier wave having a carrier-wave cycle;  
   acquiring a duty command value corresponding to a desired output of the power conversion circuit;  
   comparing the carrier wave with the duty command value;  
   operating the switching element in accordance with a result of the comparison;  
   setting an operation period during which switching operation of the switching element is determined; and  
   when the operation period is changed from a first operation period corresponding to one cycle of the carrier wave to a second operation period longer than the one cycle of the carrier wave, reducing a number of switching operations of the switching element within the second operation period.

2. The electric power control method according to claim 1, wherein reducing the number of switching operations comprises maintaining an on-state or an off-state of the switching element over a plurality of cycles of the carrier wave.

3. The electric power control method according to claim 1, wherein the switching element is operated based on the comparison between the carrier wave and the duty command value during the first operation period, and switching of the switching element is inhibited for at least one carrier-wave cycle during the second operation period.

4. The electric power control method according to claim 1, wherein the second operation period is an integer multiple of the carrier-wave cycle.

5. The electric power control method according to claim 1, wherein the number of switching operations is reduced by updating a switching command for the switching element once per the second operation period instead of once per the carrier-wave cycle.

6. The electric power control method according to claim 1, wherein the duty command value is held constant during the second operation period.

7. The electric power control method according to claim 1, wherein changing the operation period to the second operation period is performed in response to an operating condition of the power conversion circuit.

8. The electric power control method according to claim 7, wherein the operating condition includes at least one of an output power, an output current, an output voltage, a temperature of the switching element, a switching loss, or a required control response.

9. The electric power control method according to claim 1, wherein the power conversion circuit is an inverter, and the switching element is one of a plurality of switching elements operated to generate an alternating-current output.

10. The electric power control method according to claim 1, wherein reducing the number of switching operations reduces switching loss of the switching element while controlling the output of the power conversion circuit in accordance with the duty command value.
